extra_misconceptions.fact: Everyday lenses can shatter on impact; always wear ANSI Z87.1 rated safety goggles or side-shield glasses over them.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard prescription eyeglasses provide sufficient impact protection when hammering nails or cutting wood.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rotating machinery can snag glove fabric and pull fingers into the bit or wheel; keep hands bare near spinning parts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heavy work gloves improve grip and hand safety when operating a spinning bench grinder or drill press.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Particulate dust masks only trap solid fibers; organic solvent fumes require cross-ventilation or a vapor respirator.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Paper dust masks protect the lungs from toxic solvent vapors when stripping paint or applying oil varnish.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Curing oil finishes generate exothermic heat that causes spontaneous combustion; dry rags flat outdoors or submerge in water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Oily rags soaked with linseed oil or wood stain can be safely tossed into a closed shop trash bin.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to wear loose sleeves, jewelry, or knit gloves around rotating power tools?
What physical distinction separates ANSI Z87.1 impact safety glasses from everyday prescription eyewear?
What measurement confirms a ladder is set at the safe four-to-one angle against an exterior wall?
Under what condition does an extension cord's wire gauge become unsafe for a high-amp circular saw?

extra_misconceptions.fact: New caulk will not bond to loose or dirty material; scrape out all old sealant and clean the joint dry before caulking.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying a fresh bead of silicone caulk directly over cracked, peeling old caulk creates a stronger seal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wood frames expand with seasonal moisture and crack tight glass; cut panes one-eighth inch smaller and bed in compound.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting a replacement windowpane to the exact tight dimensions of the wood frame prevents drafts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dry old concrete sucks moisture out of fresh mortar before it cures; wire-brush loose debris and dampen the base first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pouring dry or wet concrete patch mix directly onto dry, dusty old concrete produces the best adhesion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A thin knife edge rolls or chips against rocks; file a single bevel at a sturdy thirty-degree angle and oil the steel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Filing both sides of a shovel or hoe blade to a razor-thin knife edge makes digging much easier.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to fresh concrete patch mortar if you trowel it into a dry, dusty masonry crack?
Which physical indicator shows that exterior window caulk has lost elasticity and needs removal?
Why must you subtract one-eighth inch from the rabbet opening when measuring a replacement glass pane?
Where should a Scout position the mill file and vise jaws when sharpening a garden spade blade?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Metal fasteners split hardwood rungs and work loose under racking loads; scrape off old glue and clamp with wood glue.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Driving metal nails or drywall screws into a loose wooden chair joint holds better than wood glue.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wood braces work in compression only when angled upward from the bottom hinge corner to the top latch rail.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A wooden gate compression brace should angle downward from the top hinge corner to the bottom latch.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Short screws only grip the thin door jamb; drive a three-inch screw through the top hinge into the framing king stud.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Short three-quarter-inch hinge screws are strong enough to keep a heavy exterior door from sagging.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heavy coats sag, drip, and wrinkle while curing; apply light coats and sand lightly with fine grit between applications.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying one thick coat of varnish or paint hides wood imperfections faster than multiple thin coats.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a diagonal compression brace run on a wooden gate frame to prevent gravity sag?
What happens to a loose chair rung joint if you apply new wood glue over hardened old glue?
What measurement confirms that a newly framed workbench top is dead level and free of wind?
Why is it dangerous to anchor a heavy stair handrail solely into drywall instead of wall studs?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ceiling boxes often contain live feed-through wires or switch loops; always shut off the circuit breaker and test voltage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Turning off the wall light switch makes it safe to replace a light fixture without shutting off the breaker.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Turning a screw clockwise pushes a counterclockwise loop outward; wrap the wire clockwise so tightening pulls it inward.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping a wire loop counterclockwise around a terminal screw holds just as tightly as clockwise.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Reversing hot and neutral energizes lamp shells and creates shock hazards; black connects to brass and white to silver.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Connecting the black hot wire to the silver screw on a polarized outlet works the same as the brass screw.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Internal spring latches must re-engage first; push the breaker handle firmly to full OFF before flipping it back to ON.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pushing a tripped circuit breaker handle directly from the middle position to ON resets the circuit.

extra_socratic_questions: Which direction must a stripped wire hook wrap around a brass terminal screw on a wall outlet?
Which physical indicator distinguishes a tripped circuit breaker handle from one switched off manually?
What measurement confirms a wall receptacle box is completely de-energized before you touch the wires?
Why is it dangerous to replace a blown fifteen-amp fuse with a twenty-amp fuse in an older panel?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hose couplings seal against a flat rubber washer and compression fittings seal on the ferrule; tape prevents full seating.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping PTFE thread seal tape around compression ferrule threads or garden hose couplings stops leaks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excessive force crushes the rubber washer and scores the brass valve seat; shut off the supply and replace the washer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cranking a dripping compression faucet handle harder and harder extends the life of the rubber washer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The curved P-trap holds a water seal that blocks toxic, flammable sewer gases like methane from entering the house.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Removing a sink P-trap permanently improves drainage speed and causes no household health hazards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Well systems rely on an electric pump and pressurized bladder tank; turn off the pump breaker and close the tank valve.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shutting off the street water valve is sufficient to stop water flow in a home supplied by a well pump.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout place a bucket and slip-joint pliers before loosening a sink P-trap union?
Which physical indicator tells you whether a running toilet has a warped flapper or a high float?
What test confirms whether water is silently leaking past a toilet tank flapper into the bowl?
Why is it dangerous to use a plunger on a sink drain after someone poured chemical cleaner inside?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gravity pulls conical plugs straight out of gypsum board; screw ceiling hooks into a wood joist or use a toggle bolt.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plastic conical wall plugs driven into hollow drywall can safely support a heavy ceiling plant hanger.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thick compound shrinks, cracks, and falls into the wall cavity; install a wood backing cleat and feather thin coats.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Filling a fist-sized drywall hole with one thick mound of spackling paste dries smooth and crack-free.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Porous joint compound absorbs paint binder and leaves a dull spot called flashing; seal patches with PVA primer first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying latex topcoat paint directly over a raw, sanded drywall patch produces a uniform wall sheen.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Leftover adhesive ridges make the replacement tile sit high and crack under foot traffic; scrape the subfloor flat first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Gluing a replacement ceramic or vinyl floor tile over crumbly old adhesive keeps the new tile level.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a four-inch drywall hole patch if you apply joint compound without a backing strip?
Under what condition does a hollow-wall toggle bolt hold more weight than a plastic expansion anchor?
What measurement confirms where the center of a wooden wall stud lies before drilling for a bracket?
Why is it dangerous to drill blindly into an interior wall without checking for aligned outlets?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Registered trade apprenticeships combine paid on-the-job field hours with classroom instruction at little or no debt.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Skilled residential trade apprentices must pay high university tuition while learning on the job.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Structural, electrical panel, and gas plumbing work require state-licensed tradespeople and municipal code inspections.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: General handymen can legally rewire main service panels or replace gas water heaters without a license.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Master licensing requires thousands of documented field hours as an apprentice and journeyman plus passing state exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing a written trade school exam alone qualifies a graduate to work as a master plumber or electrician.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most jurisdictions require permits and inspections for structural, electrical, and plumbing changes even when done by owners.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Homeowners never need a municipal building permit when performing structural or electrical repairs themselves.

extra_socratic_questions: What steps must a trade apprentice complete to advance to a licensed journeyman and master contractor?
Which legal authority separates a licensed residential electrician from an unlicensed handyman?
What hours and classroom benchmarks must an apprentice log to qualify for a state trade license exam?
Under what condition does a municipal building inspector require a permit before a repair begins?
